Already, he has forgotten about the old man in the hospital, What was his name? He looks at the faces around him, smells the sweat and akin and other human smells, and finds an empty seat. As the wheels of the bus turn, they leave behind all his old memories. Later, Edward lurches drunkenly down a forgotten up the street, stepping on and off the curb. In one hand is a street. He is laughing and muttering to himself and he weaves green bottle nearly empty, the last of twelve. He stops at the top ofa hill and lights a cigarette, crumpling and dropping the empty foil pack. He is thinking about the vigor of life, he is excited by it. Suddenly, he swings the bottle around and hurls it at the sidewalk. It collides with the edge of the curb with bitter accuracy, shattering the silence of the night. A small girl awakens and looks out her window. Edward grits his teeth and hurls the pink lighter to the pavement. It ignites with a dull thud much like the time clock that Edward has already forgotten. A gout of flame appears for the briefest moment and then is gone, leaving behind nothing but plastic shards scattered amid the ruins ofa green bottle.
